source: Table: Sample Selection Model Estimates (Generalised Two-Part Fractional Response Model)

correlation_rho.note: Not statistically significant; independent two-part model is sufficient.

participation.description: Participation equation (extensive margin): Pr(holds_ifa=1 | Z) = Phi(Z'theta). Dependent variable: holds_ifa = (ifa_ratio > 1e-3).

magnitude.description: Magnitude equation (intensive margin): E(ifa_ratio | holds_ifa=1, X, Z). Dependent variable: ifa_ratio = IFA / TFA in [0,1].

household_members_in_employment.units: count of employed adults in household

net_wealth.units: EUR / 100000 (level scaled by 1e-5, not log; net_wealth = tfa + ha - total_debt)

adjustment_parameters.note: Confirmed from frm_estimation.ipynb portfolio adjustment plot cell.

notes.se_clustering: Standard errors clustered at household id level.

scale_convention.description: Coefficients were estimated on HFCS per-household data (e.g. gross income ~EUR 30k). The INET macro model rescales each agent's financial variables by a population scale factor S (e.g. S=10 means each model agent represents 10 real households, so model income is S x HFCS income). Before applying the estimation-scale divisors below, model financial variables must first be divided by S to recover per-household real values.
scale_convention.gross_household_income: x = model_gross_income / (S * 10_000), where S is the model population scale factor
scale_convention.net_wealth: x = model_net_wealth / (S * 100_000), where S is the model population scale factor
scale_convention.unaffected_variables: age, household_size, investment_attitudes, mortgagor, owner, college, household_members_in_employment, windfall_income, wealth_quintile — these are counts, binary flags, or ordinal scales that do not scale with the model population factor

notes.model_variable_mapping_status: Units and notebook variable names confirmed against frm_estimation.ipynb.
